constructed: Section prose for the claim checker, constructed rather than captured until 6.6, because the model that writes a section arrives there. The three cause paragraphs arrived at 6.6, and two of them are the local model's own sentences from the first pass it wrote over this fixture, one cut to the fault it is kept for. Every figure in it was written against the facts file this fixture produces for KEYS on 2026-09-08, which is read back at test time from a replayed store rather than stated here, so a paragraph whose figures stopped matching would fail as a rejection nobody expected rather than pass as a copy of a number. Citations are written as the marker the checker reads, a D followed by the position of the document in the section's own source list, and each source is named by the fixture file or the constructed document it resolves to. The clean paragraphs are here beside the rejected ones on purpose: a checker that only ever saw prose written to be refused would measure nothing about what it accepts, and what it wrongly refuses is a section left out of every report. KEYS rather than AAPL, and the reason is a property of the replay: its corporate action check refetches AAPL's year as of the action's own session, so AAPL's stored series ends on 2026-08-10 and the replay writes no facts file for it on the fixture night at all. KEYS is refetched by nothing and holds the same facts file in every chain the suite replays.

sections.name: a clean computed paragraph
sections.prose: Keysight closed at 333.42, above its 50-day average of 326.21 and well above the 200-day average of 289.31. Revenue for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was $1.85 billion, with a gross margin of 65.9% and a net margin of 21.5%. The shares trade at 45.9 times trailing earnings of 7.38 a share.
sections.carries: every figure a rounding of one the facts file holds, at the precision the prose itself states: 326.21 of 326.213, $1.85 billion of 1846000000.00, 65.9% of a margin stored as the fraction 0.658722, and 45.9 of 45.8862. Two window lengths, which are numbers the facts file carries in the names of its averages rather than in their values, and one date. No citation, because this is the one section the lane table says is written from known values with nothing to weigh.

sections.name: a poisoned paragraph
sections.prose: Keysight closed at 333.42, above its 50-day average of 326.21 and well above the 200-day average of 289.31. Revenue for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was $1.85 billion, with a gross margin of 66.3% and a net margin of 21.5%. The shares trade at 45.9 times trailing earnings of 7.38 a share.
sections.carries: the clean paragraph above with one figure changed, a gross margin of 66.3% where the facts file holds 0.658722. A near miss rather than an absurd figure, 0.43 of a point from the true margin, because the wrong figure a writer produces is a slip of rounding far more often than an invention, and a poison further away would be refused by a checker that had stopped reading the precision the prose states. One and only one, so the rejection is asserted to name exactly that figure rather than to have found something wrong somewhere in a paragraph of eleven.

sections.name: a clean researched paragraph
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Revenue for the July quarter was $1.85 billion [D1].
sections.carries: a citation on every sentence, resolving to the release exhibit the filings archive holds, which is admitted, and one figure that is also in the facts file. A claim resting on a document has to name it and a figure in it has to be one code computed, and this paragraph satisfies both halves so neither can be what the rejections below turn on.

sections.name: an unsourced claim
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Analysts expect the next design cycle to be the strongest in five years.
sections.carries: the same first sentence and a second that names no document at all. It carries no digit, so the number rule has nothing to say about it and the citation rule is the only thing that can refuse it, which is the shape of a confident wrong sentence the decision is about.

sections.name: a claim resting on a refused document
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Its test business is expected to keep growing faster than its software [D2].
sections.carries: a citation that resolves to a stored row admissibility refused. The document is stored, so a rule asking only whether a source exists would pass it, and the claim checker reads the verdict on the row rather than applying the test again, which 6.0 ruled.

sections.name: a section with no admissible source
sources: inadmissible: a page with no publish date
sections.carries: a section whose whole source list was refused, which is what a pass leaves when it fetched documents and admitted none of them. It goes to fallback on the first check rather than being given a retry, because a rewrite cannot create a source, and what the name page draws for it is one line saying no admissible source was found.

sections.name: a cause citing a release filed after the move
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: The largest move, of 28.62 per cent, ended on 2026-02-24 and was driven by the company reporting third quarter revenue of $1.85 billion [D1].
sections.carries: the first draft a local model wrote for this section at 6.6, with the one date it quoted that the facts file does not hold taken out so that only the rule this paragraph is for can refuse it. Every figure is a rounding of a fact and the citation resolves to an admitted document, which is everything the checker asked of a sentence before 6.6. What it states is false: the release was filed on 2026-08-18 and the move it is cited for was measured from 2026-02-17 to 2026-02-24.

sections.name: a cause naming no move
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: Keysight shares moved on record third quarter revenue of $1.85 billion [D1].
sections.carries: a cause with a citation and a sound figure that names no stored move's session, so nothing says which move it is about and no span exists to hold its document against.

sections.name: a cause of the move the release falls inside
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: The move from 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-24 was driven by record third quarter results with revenue of $1.85 billion and GAAP net income of $397 million, as detailed in the results release exhibit [D1].
sections.carries: the sentence the local model wrote on its first draft once the writer handed it the one move the release falls inside, captured at 6.6 and accepted: the release was filed on 2026-08-18, inside the move measured from 2026-08-17 and ended on 2026-08-24. Accepted is not the same as true, and this paragraph carries that too: the checker holds when the document was published and every figure in the sentence, and not that a company's own release says why its shares fell.

attempts.name: rejected twice
attempts.carries: the retry bound. The second attempt fails as the first did, so the section goes to fallback with both attempts' offending text kept, the first on its own rejected row and the second on the fallback row, and no third attempt is checked as a retry of either.

attempts.name: rejected then accepted
attempts.carries: the retry doing what it is for, so the bound is not asserted over a checker that simply refuses every second attempt.
